CAS — 64-18-6. ATC Vet — QP53AG01. Pharmacopoeias. In Pol. Profile Formic acid resembles acetic acid in its properties (see p.2244) but is more irritating and pungent. The acid and its sodium and calcium salts are used as preservatives in food. Solutions con- taining about 60% formic acid have been marketed for the re- moval of lime scale from kettles. Formic acid has also been used for the removal of tattoos. It is an ingredient of some external preparations promoted for the relief of musculoskeletal and joint disorders, and has been used with benzyl alcohol to aid the re- moval of nits. ◊ In a report of 3 patients who swallowed descaling agents con- taining 40 or 55% formic acid, the major complications included local corrosive effects, metabolic acidosis, derangement of blood-clotting mechanisms, and acute onset of respiratory and renal failure.1 All 3 patients died between 5 and 14 days after admission to hospital. A further report of 53 cases of formic acid ingestion included 15 fatalities.2 1. Naik RB, et al. Ingestion of formic acid-containing agents — report of three fatal cases. Postgrad Med J 1980; 56: 451–6. 2. Rajan N, et al. Formic acid poisoning with suicidal intent: a re- port of 53 cases. Postgrad Med J 1985; 61: 35–6.
